correctness.rationale: For arbitrary positive-definite \(Q\), sign averaging preserves every two-sided comparison with the unconditional Nakano norm and removes off-diagonal entries, so diagonal ellipses suffice. On the unit sphere the squared diagonal form is \(F_r(t)=1-t^m+rt\). Its endpoint minimum and unique critical maximum give an explicit distortion ratio, whose derivative is negative on \(0<r\le1\) and whose remaining branches increase from \(r=1\). Thus \(r=1\) is the global minimizer and the displayed formula follows for every \(q>2\). No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a closed exact Hilbert-distortion benchmark for a classical non-permutation-symmetric one-parameter family of finite-dimensional Nakano spaces. The exponent pair \((2,q)\) is the simplest genuinely variable-exponent deformation away from Hilbert geometry, and the theorem identifies the globally optimal ellipsoid and its extremal contact directions for every \(q>2\).
